sections.html:
Kearns occupies 4.63 square miles of the valley's west side, hemmed in by West Valley City, Taylorsville and West Jordan. Its 36,723 residents in 2020 worked out to about 7,932 per square mile, and the July 2025 estimate is 35,404. With houses this close together, a vacant or run-down one shows from the street.

Kearns began in 1942 as Kearns Army Air Base, and developers built homes on the former base land after the war. Much of the housing went up between the mid and late 20th century, so original roofs, wiring and plumbing are common. Buyers tend to ask first how old those systems are.

Cityhood arrived on May 1, 2024, following years as an unincorporated community, a township and a metro township. Daily services still come from shared providers: Unified Police and Unified Fire for public safety, and the Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District for building permits, business licensing, land use and zoning, code enforcement and stormwater.

For permit questions, visit 860 W. Levoy Dr., Suite 300, Taylorsville, or call 385-910-5600. The mayor's office takes visits by appointment at 4250 W 5415 S, phone 385-855-8375. The city has gained more tax options as a result of incorporation, including a property tax and a telecommunications tax, so watch the city's budget and agenda pages if future taxes matter to you.

Granite School District schools serve the area, including Kearns High School. Oquirrh Park holds the Utah Olympic Oval at 5662 South Cougar Lane, built in 2001 for the 2002 Winter Olympics, where the public can skate and take classes. A new Kearns Library opened in December 2020. A buyer comparing neighborhoods may like hearing about these.

Summers are warm and mostly dry; winters are cold. Salt Lake County gets roughly 15 inches of precipitation and 55 inches of snow in a typical year, and that works the roof and furnace hard. Find out how old both are before anyone asks.

Utah's most active fault, the Wasatch, runs nearby. Liquefaction risk is highest where a valley floor is low and groundwater shallow, particularly close to lakes and streams, and the soils at risk are loose, young, sandy or silty layers saturated within about 30 to 50 feet of the surface. Kearns sits on the old Lake Bonneville bed, so looking up your lot on the Utah Geological Survey maps is sensible.

  • The maps show general patterns only.
  • A single lot needs a site study by a qualified engineer and geologist.
  • The Salt Lake City segment last produced a large quake about 1,400 years back.

Property tax on a Kearns house goes to Salt Lake County. Miss November 30 and the balance is delinquent from December 1. Each parcel is valued as of January 1.

Tax calendar dateWhat happens
January 1Assessed value locks in
July and AugustValuation notices arrive
July 31 to September 15Appeals accepted
By November 1Tax notices are mailed
November 30Final day to pay with no penalty
May or JuneTax sales of parcels delinquent over five years

Only this year's market value can go before the Board of Equalization, and the bill stays payable while an appeal is pending. Good evidence is a recent purchase, a fee appraisal, or three to five comparable sales. Ask the Treasurer at 385-468-8300 about tax relief programs.

The 45% primary residential exemption leaves a main residence taxed on 55% of its value, but only if someone lives there at least 183 consecutive days in a year. After a sale, the new owner files a fresh claim.

sections.h2: Closing a cash sale in Kearns
sections.html:
Closing happens through a title or escrow company, and the Salt Lake County Recorder at 2001 South State Street records the deed for a flat $40. Expect the deed to need a county legal description, the parcel number and an original notarized signature.

  • Print the buyer's mailing address on the deed.
  • Submit the deed on white 8.5 by 11 paper with a blank strip at the top of page one.
  • Mailed originals return in roughly two to three weeks.
  • Recorder staff cannot draft or notarize; call 385-468-8145 with questions.

The title company usually takes care of this, though you should confirm that names on the deed match the signature page. A mortgage payoff or tax balance is paid from your proceeds at closing, and the remainder is yours.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale right for an older Kearns house?
sections.html:
Options include an agent listing, a private sale and a cash offer. A listing asks you to prep the house, pay commission and wait on a buyer's loan. With cash, the house sells as it is and you have a say in the closing date.

  • Postwar-era houses whose original systems need replacing.
  • Inherited homes where the family cannot take on repairs.
  • Rentals where tenants make showings difficult.
  • Owners behind on payments who need a firm timeline.

With any buyer, ask for the closing date and proof of funds in writing, then measure the offer against what a listing would net.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or tenant-occupied house
sections.html:
Two situations come up often in older neighborhoods like these. With an inherited house, the title search has to show who now owns it, so the court or estate papers matter more than anything else you bring. Family members who live far away can usually sign before a notary where they are and mail the pages back, which keeps one person from having to handle everything.

With a tenant in place, the lease terms decide how a sale can go. Showings for a regular listing are hard to schedule around someone else's home, while a cash buyer can look at the house once and does not need repeated visits. Tell us early what the lease says about notice and end dates, so closing is set for a day that works for everyone involved.

sections.h2: What buyers ask about older Kearns houses
sections.html: Expect questions about the roof, the furnace and air conditioner, the water heater, the electrical panel and the sewer line, since many houses still have their original versions. Photos of each, with the year of any replacement, let a buyer judge the house quickly. Mention past leaks, additions and finished basements too, and have the permit records ready. A buyer paying cash can price all of this in, while a buyer using a loan may need repairs finished first.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html: The process is short. Start by telling us the address, the house's age and any failing systems. We compare it with nearby sales and make an offer. Say yes, and a title company searches the record, confirms what is owed and books signing. After you sign, the deed is recorded and funds go out to you. Nobody holds an open house or waits for a bank, and a later closing date is fine if you need time to move. Before any of this, collect your deed, a mortgage statement and the latest tax notice.

faqs.q: Is Kearns a city or a township?
faqs.a: A city, since May 1, 2024. Before that it was a township and then a metro township, and many services still run through the Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District.

faqs.q: Who handles building permits in Kearns?
faqs.a: The Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District, at 385-910-5600. It also covers business licensing, land use, zoning, code enforcement and stormwater.

faqs.q: What is the property tax deadline in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: November 30, with delinquency from December 1. Appeals are heard between July 31 and September 15.

faqs.q: Does Kearns have its own police and fire department?
faqs.a: Police and fire service come from Unified Police and Unified Fire.

faqs.q: How many people live in Kearns?
faqs.a: 36,723 in 2020, and an estimated 35,404 as of July 1, 2025.
